- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model may overfit upward trend; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast if price is >10% above 14d moving average.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 1–3% per day lagged from prior 7d average.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction of 1–2% per 3–5 day window after sentiment shift.
- Avoid forecasting above 10% above recent 14d high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., >3 consecutive 1.00s); cap at 10% below 14d high if sentiment drops.
